permissions.__defaultMode_options: Options: (unset)=ask-every-time, 'dontAsk'=allow-list-only, 'auto'=AI-classifier, 'bypassPermissions'=no-checks. BEGINNERS: leave unset (delete the defaultMode line) so Claude asks permission for every action until you trust your setup.
permissions.__defaultMode_WARNING: dontAsk silently denies unlisted tools with no error message. New users should remove this line and learn the permission system before enabling it.
permissions.__additionalDirectories_note: Replace paths below with YOUR home directory. Windows: C:\Users\YourUser\.claude | macOS: /Users/youruser/.claude | Linux: /home/youruser/.claude. Tilde (~) is NOT supported here; use full absolute paths.

environment: Cloud provider(s): YOUR_CLOUD (e.g., AWS, GCP, Azure)

SessionStart.__compact_note: Runs after every compaction (auto or manual). SessionStart stdout becomes context Claude reads, so this restores the working habits the summary may have dropped. Inline on purpose: no script, so every preset keeps it.

hooks.command: echo 'Context was just compacted. 1) Check your todo list and resume the in-progress item. 2) Re-read the active plan file if one exists. 3) Rules from CLAUDE.md still apply; re-read it if you are unsure of one. 4) If ~/.claude/precompact-state.json or ~/.claude/session-checkpoint.txt exists (the full and standard presets write them), read it before continuing.'

PreToolUse.__guard_note: Full preset. Keeps read-only agents (permissionMode: plan) read-only in every permission mode. Set AGENT_WRITE_GUARD_AGENTS in env to change the list.
Full preset, paired with the self-audit skill. Denies ExitPlanMode until the plan file carries AUDIT CLEAN.

Stop.__judge_note: One Sonnet call per response checks security and that a done/fixed/verified claim carries its own evidence. Labelled cases: tests/judge-fixtures/, replayed by tests/judge-eval.sh (manual, needs an API key).
Stop.__cost_note: This Stop hook runs Sonnet on EVERY response. In a 50-response session, this adds ~50 Sonnet calls (cost impact: see TROUBLESHOOTING.md#cost-is-higher-than-expected). Remove if cost is a concern.

hooks.prompt: You judge one message: the assistant's final message of this turn, given as last_assistant_message in the hook input below. You cannot see tool calls, files or earlier turns, so judge only the text of that message. Respond with JSON only: {"ok": true} or {"ok": false, "reason": "concise description of the issue"}. If the message is plain conversation or explanation, with no code and no claim that work is done, fixed, passing, deployed or verified, respond {"ok": true} immediately. A progress note that names work still running and calls nothing done is plain conversation. Otherwise flag ONLY these, judged from the visible text: 1) Security: code in the message with SQL injection, XSS or command injection, or a credential value (password, token, API key, private key) written out literally. Saying a credential exists is fine. 2) The message reports a git push that breaks a push policy it states or quotes (for example a direct push to a protected main branch). 3) Claim without evidence: the message says work is done, fixed, shipped, passing or verified, but does not itself carry the evidence: no command with its result, no test count or exit code, no URL or endpoint checked with what it returned, no re-read of the changed file. Evidence that appeared earlier in the turn but is not repeated in this message does not count: the final report must carry its own evidence, because it is what the user reads. A claim that a result is verified while the message also says the check is still running or pending is flagged too. Not flagged: a message that states plainly that a check could not be run and why (for example there is no test suite, or the server is unreachable), or that the work is not yet verified. If what you flag cannot be fixed by the assistant at all (it needs the user, or a system the assistant cannot reach), add "impossible": true so the turn can end. Anything you cannot see is not a violation; when unsure, respond {"ok": true}. Your answer must match your finding: if your reason would say there is no violation, respond {"ok": true}.
